Message from the Dean

Where innovation meets impact

Dr. Turki N. BaroudDean, KFUPM Business School

At KFUPM Business School, we are reimagining business education for a new era defined by innovation, technology, and purpose.

As Saudi Arabia advances toward Vision 2030, KBS is shaping leaders who can bridge business and technology, turning ideas into real-world impact. Our programs empower students to think strategically, act entrepreneurially, and lead responsibly in a fast-changing global economy.

We believe that true business leadership today requires fluency in data, technology, and systems thinking, coupled with a deep sense of purpose and responsibility toward society.

Our faculty combine world-class scholarship with industry engagement, ensuring that every course, project, and partnership connects classroom learning with real business challenges. Through our global collaborations and deep ties to industry, we are building a learning ecosystem that equips graduates not just to adapt to change but to lead it. KBS will continue to evolve, expanding interdisciplinary programs, advancing impactful research, and fostering an entrepreneurial mindset among students and executives alike.

Department Chairman

Dr. Rabih Nehme

Chairman, Department of Accounting & Finance · Associate Professor of Accounting

KFUPM Business School

BS Finance and Financial Engineering

Model the markets. Manage the risk. Engineer the outcome.

Source: KBSBS Finance & Financial Engineering05
Overview

Program Overview

  • Prepares quantitatively skilled professionals to analyze financial markets, value financial instruments, and support investment and risk management decisions
  • Integrates finance theory, mathematics, statistics, and analytical methods to explain financial market behavior, value financial instruments, and apply rigorous models in financial decision-making
  • Equips graduates to assess investment opportunities, evaluate financial products, and use quantitative tools widely applied in trading, portfolio management, and financial analysis
Disciplines and competencies covered
Financial markets
Quantitative methods
Machine learning
Risk management
Source: KBSBS Finance & Financial Engineering06
Program Learning Outcomes

What You Will Learn

01

BS Finance and Financial Engineering

Graduates will be able to demonstrate the following knowledge, skills, and values

Knowledge and Understanding
Principles of financial markets and financial instruments
Mathematical finance concepts, including the quantitative methods used in financial analysis and decision making
Skills
Use financial software and technological tools to implement and test financial models
Apply mathematical and statistical tools to analyze financial data and decisions
Evaluate the adequacy of risk measurement models and analyze their results
Communicate financial solutions effectively, both orally and in writing
Work effectively in collaborative and inclusive teams, and lead teams working on financial problems
Values, Autonomy, and Responsibility
Demonstrate professional and ethical responsibility in global financial analysis and decision making through appropriate judgment and conduct
Acquire and apply new knowledge as needed, using appropriate self-learning strategies
Source: KBSBS Finance & Financial Engineering07
BS Finance and Financial Engineering

Where markets, mathematics and machine intelligence connect

  • A new quantitative-finance engineering program for the next generation of financial talent
  • Mathematical content is geared toward skills used in financial applications: trading, portfolio management, and financial analysis
  • Builds capabilities in time series, credit risk, derivatives, machine learning and algorithmic trading
Career pathways
Investment & riskQuantitative analysisAlgorithmic tradingPortfolio managementHedge fundsCredit riskDerivatives
Source: KBSBS Finance & Financial Engineering08
BS Finance and Financial Engineering

Career Prospects

01Investment / Risk Analyst

Evaluates financial market trends, assesses potential risks and supports smart investment decisions

02Quantitative Analyst

Uses mathematical models and advanced data to predict market movements and develop systematic trading tools

03Algorithmic Trader / Broker

Executes automated trades using computer-driven models to optimize speed and efficiency

04Portfolio Manager

Directs the buying and selling of investment assets to meet the goals of clients or firms

05Stock Analyst / Data Analyst in Finance

Gathers and interprets financial data to support business decisions and stock market investments

06Hedge Fund Strategy Analyst

Conducts deep market research to develop and test specialized investment strategies

07Investment, Risk or Credit Risk Analyst

Reviews financial health, measures lending or investment risks and ensures safe financial practices

08Financial Engineer / Derivatives Analyst

Designs new financial products and risk-management tools that protect companies against market shifts

Source: KBSBS Finance & Financial Engineering09
BS Finance and Financial Engineering · Practical training

Summer Training & Internship

Every student gains real workplace experience before graduating. The degree plan comes in two tracks, so you choose how you get it: a summer training placement or a full-semester internship.

BS Finance and Financial Engineering course descriptions
Core

Financial Management

FIN 250
Pre-requisiteACCT 110, ECON 102Topics9
  • Basic concepts of finance
  • Time value of money and conceptual framework of risk and return. Overview of financial markets and institutions
  • Financial statements
  • Ratio analysis
  • Cash flow analysis
  • Capital budgeting techniques
  • Security valuation
  • The cost of capital
  • Techniques of financial planning and analysis and working capital management
Source: KBSBS Finance & Financial Engineering15
BS Finance and Financial Engineering course descriptions
Core

Foundations of Econometrics

ECON 205
Pre-requisiteECON 102, STAT 214Topics4
  • Practical and conceptual issues involved in substantive applications of econometric techniques
  • Analysis of estimation & inference procedures for simple econometric models
  • Empirical case studies using real-life data
  • Linear regression models and its diagnostics
Source: KBSBS Finance & Financial Engineering16
BS Finance and Financial Engineering course descriptions
Core

Corporate Finance

FIN 315
Pre-requisiteFIN 250Topics7
  • The theory and practice of financial decisions and their interaction to determine the firm’s value
  • Capital investment decisions with certainty and under risk
  • Financing decision through capital structure theory, cost of capital
  • The dividends policy choices with implications
  • The management of working capital and short-term financing
  • Valuation of securities
  • Real options analysis, leasing, mergers and acquisitions, agency theory and corporate governance
Source: KBSBS Finance & Financial Engineering17
BS Finance and Financial Engineering course descriptions
NewCore

Security Analysis and Portfolio Optimization

FFE 335
Pre-requisiteFIN 250, STAT 214Topics5
  • Security analysis and portfolio optimization
  • Valuation of equities, bonds, other financial assets using fundamental and quantitative approaches
  • Application of modern portfolio theory to risk-return trade-offs
  • Use of financial data, performance measures, optimization techniques
  • Construction of efficient investment portfolios and support of practical investment decision-making
Source: KBSBS Finance & Financial Engineering18
BS Finance and Financial Engineering course descriptions
NewCore

Time Series Analysis & Statistical Arbitrage

FFE 320
Pre-requisiteECON 205Topics5
  • Time series analysis and its application to statistical arbitrage in financial markets
  • Statistical properties of financial data including trends, seasonality, and volatility
  • Application of econometric and quantitative techniques for modeling and forecasting asset prices
  • Design and evaluation of data-driven trading strategies based on mean reversion, cointegration, relative value
  • Practical analysis of real financial time series
Source: KBSBS Finance & Financial Engineering19
BS Finance and Financial Engineering course descriptions
NewCore

Interest Rates and Credit Risk Modeling

FFE 336
Pre-requisiteFIN 315, FFE 335Topics6
  • Modeling and analysis of interest rates and credit risk
  • Behavior of interest rates, term structure models, and yield curves
  • Quantitative approaches to measuring and managing credit risk
  • Application of mathematical and statistical techniques to real financial data
  • Pricing of bonds and credit-sensitive instruments
  • Assessment of default risk and support of risk management, investment decisions in financial institutions
Source: KBSBS Finance & Financial Engineering20
BS Finance and Financial Engineering course descriptions
NewCore

Case Studies in Investment and Technical Analysis

FFE 337
Pre-requisiteFFE 335Topics7
  • Application of investment theory and technical analysis through real-world case studies
  • Ethical decision-making in investment management
  • Advising individual and institutional investors
  • Long-term wealth management strategies
  • Short-term tactical trading with emphasis on technical analysis
  • Portfolio construction and evaluation
  • Disciplined investment decision-making aligned with professional standards
Source: KBSBS Finance & Financial Engineering21
BS Finance and Financial Engineering course descriptions
Core

Futures and Options Markets

FIN 460
Pre-requisiteFIN 320 OR FFE 335Topics4
  • Derivative securities and their markets
  • The regulatory framework for financial derivatives and the operations of derivatives exchanges
  • The characteristics of futures and option contracts and their associated trading strategies for achieving risk-return objectives
  • Arbitrage principles and pricing of derivative securities
Source: KBSBS Finance & Financial Engineering22
BS Finance and Financial Engineering course descriptions
NewCore

Machine Learning in Finance

FFE 333
Pre-requisiteCOE 292, FIN 315Topics12
  • Machine learning techniques and their applications in financial analysis and decision making
  • Financial Data Sources, Data Cleaning, Feature Engineering
  • Supervised learning
  • Unsupervised learning
  • Classification Methods
  • Credit Scoring
  • Bankruptcy Prediction
  • Fraud Detection
  • Ensemble Methods, Bagging, Boosting, XGBoost
  • Dimensionality Reduction, Clustering, PCA
  • Predictive Analytics
  • Credit Risk Modeling, Loan Default Prediction
Source: KBSBS Finance & Financial Engineering23
BS Finance and Financial Engineering course descriptions
NewCore

Quantitative Risk Management

FFE 338
Pre-requisiteMATH 208, STAT 214, FFE 335Topics5
  • Quantitative methods for measuring, modeling, and managing financial risk
  • Analysis of market, credit, and operational risks
  • Application of statistical and mathematical techniques to real financial data
  • Use of risk metrics, simulation methods, and stress testing
  • Support of risk management practices and regulatory compliance in financial institutions

BS Finance and Financial Engineering course descriptions
NewCore

Market Microstructure and Algo Trading

FFE 440
Pre-requisiteMATH 208, FFE 335Topics6
  • Market microstructure and trading mechanisms
  • Order-driven markets, price formation, and liquidity
  • Design and evaluation of algorithmic trading strategies
  • Analysis of transaction costs and execution risk
  • Impact of trading algorithms on market quality
  • Practical analysis of high-frequency and intraday market data
